title: Boss: filters for the log pipeline
summary: The platform team is moving to a new log shipper that takes one regex per rule. Write the drop filter, the metric extractor, the branch policy and the card-number mask.

steps.title: The ticket
body: **PLAT-219: rules for the new log pipeline.** The shipper gives each rule **one pattern field** (it runs .NET
regex), with no invert option and no code. The rules:
1. **Drop** health checks: keep only lines that do not hit `/healthz` or `/readyz`.
2. **Extract** the request duration in milliseconds as a metric, the number only.
3. **Tag** builds by the ticket in the branch name, and reject branches that break the naming policy.
4. **Mask** card numbers before anything is stored (PCI DSS: show at most the last four digits).
Rules 3 and 4 also run in the C# ingestion service, so they are written as methods.

steps.title: Drop the health checks
prompt: With Multiline on, match each **whole line** to keep: every line that does not request `/healthz` or `/readyz`.
Those names are whole path segments: `/readyzone` is a real endpoint and must be kept.

all.input:
GET /healthz 200 2ms
GET /orders/42 200 87ms
GET /readyz 200 1ms
POST /pay 503 1200ms
GET /readyzone 200 5ms
GET /api/healthz?full=1 200 9ms

steps.title: Extract the duration metric
prompt: Lines carry `key=value` fields. The metric is the number in `duration=<n>ms`, and the match must be **the number
only** (the shipper stores the whole match). `duration=7s` is in seconds and does not count, and
`predicted_duration=` is a different field. Use a lookbehind for the field name and a lookahead for the unit.

require.message: Uses a lookbehind for the field name
Uses a lookahead for the unit

steps.title: The branch naming policy
prompt: Write `string? TicketOfBranch(string branch)`. A valid branch name is, in this order:
- a type: `feature`, `fix` or `chore`, then `/`
- a ticket key: 2 to 5 capital letters, `-`, digits
- `-` and a slug of lowercase letters, digits and dashes
and anywhere in it, no `--`, and it does not end with `-`. Return the ticket key for a valid name, `null` otherwise.
| branch | result |
| `feature/OPS-311-retry-payments` | `OPS-311` |
| `hotfix/OPS-1-x` | `null` |
| `feature/OPS-311-retry--payments` | `null` |
Use one pattern: alternation for the type, a named group for the ticket, negative lookaheads for the two
"anywhere" rules. `System.Text.RegularExpressions` is already imported.
template: Dojo.Eq("hotfix is not an allowed type", (string?)null, TicketOfBranch("hotfix/OPS-1-x"));
Dojo.Eq("the ticket key is in capitals", (string?)null, TicketOfBranch("feature/ops-311-retry"));

steps.title: Mask card numbers
prompt: Write `string MaskCards(string text)`. Every run of **13 to 19** digits is a card number: replace each of its
digits with `*`, except the last four. Shorter and longer runs of digits (order ids, trace ids) stay as they are.
| text | result |
Any correct approach passes. The neat one is a single `Regex.Replace` with `"*"` as the replacement, where the
pattern matches one digit that has at least four digits after it, inside a run of the right length (a lookbehind
may contain a lookahead in .NET). `System.Text.RegularExpressions` is already imported.
solution: // A digit with 4+ digits after it, inside a run that starts at a non-digit and is 13-19 digits long.
template: Dojo.Eq("two cards in one line", "two cards ************5556 and ************4444", MaskCards("two cards 4000056655665556 and 5555555555554444"));
Dojo.Eq("13 digits is a card", "*********2222", MaskCards("4222222222222"));
Dojo.Eq("short and long runs stay", "order 123456 trace 12345678901234567890", MaskCards("order 123456 trace 12345678901234567890"));
Dojo.Eq("no digits, no change", "nothing to hide", MaskCards("nothing to hide"));
